# IdeaVim fixtures this host does not match yet.
#
# Generated by VimFixtureReplayTest, which writes the current list to
# build/fixture-failures.txt with the difference for each one, and a header saying how many were
# harvested and why the rest were not. To update this file, read that one and copy the names across
# - never edit a name by hand to make the build pass. A comment here is a whole line: a fixture's
# name can contain `#`, because the second `doTest` in a method is `...#2`.
#
# 2414 of the 2423 harvested fixtures pass.
#
# Nine of the twenty arrived with the corpus's fifth step - `commandToKeys` and the read-only
# assertions - and they are what a new fixture is for. Six are one gap: a mapping onto a *modified*
# Escape or Enter never fires, so `:nmap <A-Esc> k` then `<A-Esc>` does nothing. Two are the
# insert-mode undo caret, one column out, which is the family `<C-T>` and `<C-D>` were already in.
# The last names an IntelliJ action, like the five below it.
#
# The corpus has grown from 1,047 to 2,081 in four steps, and every one of them was the harness
# looking at less of `src/test` than it thought: it only found backtick-quoted test names, it only
# read a method whose body *started* with `doTest`, it skipped the extension tests wholesale, and it
# only read `doTest` at all - where 922 of IdeaVim's tests are written as `configureByText` /
# `typeText` / `assertState`, which is what `doTest` is a helper over.
#
# What the corpus has found is worth more than the count. Nine real gaps in this host, every one
# fixed; two fixtures that were `@Disabled` in the plugin and never passed there either; and order
# dependence, because `VimSearchGroupBase` keeps four fields in a `protected companion object` and
# every fixture was being replayed into whatever its neighbour had left behind.
#
# The largest was `u`. It undid a keystroke where Vim undoes a command - `ciwfoo<Esc>u` put back
# `fo` - because this host writes to VS Code once per keystroke and VS Code's default is an undo
# stop around every edit an extension makes. 128 fixtures said so at once. See `UndoStops`.


# --- IntelliJ actions, which this host has no equivalent of.
#
# `ideajoin` is IntelliJ's language-aware join. The rest name an action id with no VS Code command
# behind it - `EditorDown`, `EditorCloneCaretBelow`, `EditorSelectWord`, `EditorToggleCase`.
#
# The sixth step - Guava's list builder, and a `val` bound to a list - added 234 fixtures and three
# failures, and all three are one bug: `g;` and `g,` with a count land one column late. `999g;`
# should reach the oldest change at offset 0 and reaches 1. IdeaVim passes them, so the change list
# here is recording a position after the edit rather than at it.
#
# The seventh step - a dollar the source escaped - added 22 and found five more. Four were the
# `g;` bug, and all seven of those are fixed: the `.` mark was being set past the change rather
# than at it. What is left of that step is `$hlj`, where `$` should leave the intended column at
# end-of-line and this host keeps the real one.
#
# The six `<A-Esc>`/`<S-Enter>` mapping fixtures were never a host gap. They were this harness
# reading `commandToKeys` as `exCommand`: the first types its body and the second parses it, so
# `nmap <A-Esc> k` was pressing Alt+Escape on the command line instead of writing five characters
# into it, and the mapping was never defined. Recorded here as a host bug for two steps.
#
# The two shift fixtures were named for undo and failed before any undo: `<C-T>` in Insert mode
# indented the line and left the caret behind. The engine moves no caret there on purpose, because
# IntelliJ's are document markers and the edit carries them; this host holds carets as values and
# was shifting only the *other* ones.
#
# The two `<C-U>` fixtures were the host re-reading its carets only when a command had changed the
# text. `u` there restores an identical document and a different caret, so nothing was read back.
